skim: An Indonesian ferry, the Virgo Transport 8, capsized in the Java Sea early Sunday with as many as 129 people still missing off Borneo’s coast, after only 108 of roughly 243 aboard were rescued and 6 bodies recovered.

Sweden’s centre-left opposition narrowly edged Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing coalition 175 seats to 174, denying the surging Sweden Democrats the government role many had billed as a historic breakthrough.

Oman indefinitely postponed a Salalah summit meant to ease the Strait of Hormuz standoff after drone strikes on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and new attacks near Qeshm Island, as Yemen’s government forces counterattacked Houthi positions along the Red Sea coast.

Anthropic agreed to buy $13.7 billion in GPU computing services from Tether-linked RUM Group over six years, even as Nvidia was reported to be in talks to anchor Anthropic’s own IPO with up to $10 billion at a potential $2 trillion valuation.
India beat Sri Lanka by 73 runs in Dubai to win a record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, avenging their 2024 final defeat to the same opponents.

stories.headline: Indonesian Ferry Capsizes in Java Sea, About 129 Missing
stories.body: The passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8, a 119-meter, Japan-built vessel carrying a manifest of 243 people from Surabaya to Banjarmasin, capsized in the Java Sea before dawn Sunday after its captain reported waves up to three meters and radioed a distress call, per NPR (Sep 13). At least six bodies have been recovered and 108 people rescued, with roughly 129 still missing as crews search the strait; “It is extremely risky for vessels — even our Basarnas vessel, which is 40 metres long, is at great risk,” said I Putu Sudayana, head of the Banjarmasin search and rescue office.

stories.headline: Sweden’s Centre-Left Edges Ahead in Knife-Edge Election, Blocking Far Right
stories.body: Sweden’s opposition bloc, headed by Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson, narrowly outpolled PM Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing coalition 175 seats to 174 in the 349-seat Riksdag, with the Social Democrats taking about 28% of the vote to finish as the largest single party, per Euronews (Sep 14). The wafer-thin margin denies the Sweden Democrats — who placed third on 17.6%, behind the Moderates’ 19.9% — the cabinet role their surge in support had been billed as a historic breakthrough toward, though official results and a week of tense coalition talks still lie ahead.

stories.headline: Philippines Digs Mass Grave as Ferry Fire Identifications Lag
stories.body: Only 5 of the 76 confirmed dead from the MV June Aster ferry fire off Coron, Palawan, had been identified as of Sunday, prompting President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to order forensic teams to speed up the work, per Philstar (Sep 14). A disaster-victim identification team from Camp Crame is now extracting molar teeth for DNA testing and local officials have dug a mass grave at San Nicolas Public Cemetery to temporarily hold unidentified remains; “We must mobilize the specialists, resources and funding needed to identify the victims quickly and accurately,” said Cabinet Secretary Benhur Abalos.

stories.headline: Amazon Cuts Ties With Cargo Carrier After Fatal Miami Crash
stories.body: Amazon announced Sunday it is suspending operations with 21 Air, the carrier behind the Boeing 767 that overran a runway and crashed at Miami International Airport on Sept. 6, killing five people, per UPI (Sep 13). “Safety has always been our top priority, whether in our operations or when we’re working with partners,” said Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel, while 21 Air responded it remains “confident in our safety policies, procedures and training” as the NTSB continues analyzing the jet’s recovered black boxes.

stories.headline: Haaland’s Disputed Strike Sinks 10-Man United in Manchester Derby
stories.body: Erling Haaland’s goal — initially flagged offside but restored by VAR after officials ruled a City teammate never played the ball — gave Manchester City a 1-0 win at Old Trafford, per NBC Sports (Sep 13). Phil Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute for kicking Bruno Fernandes, leaving City to see out over an hour a man light; Haaland called it “kind of a new experience to win down to 10 men.”

stories.headline: Antonelli Snatches Spanish GP Win on Strategy as Norris Fumes
stories.body: Kimi Antonelli won the Spanish Grand Prix at Madring, beating pole-sitter Lando Norris’ qualifying advantage after a Virtual Safety Car and a slow McLaren pit stop flipped the race, finishing ahead of Max Verstappen and Norris, per Formula1.com (Sep 13). It was Antonelli’s eighth win of the season, stretching his championship lead to 81 points, though he admitted “I think Lando today deserved to win.”

stories.headline: India Rout Sri Lanka to Claim Record Eighth Women’s Asia Cup
stories.body: India beat Sri Lanka by 73 runs in Dubai to win the Women’s Asia Cup final, posting 183/5 behind Shafali Verma’s 68 and a half-century from Smriti Mandhana before Shree Charani (4 wickets) and Deepti Sharma (3) skittled Sri Lanka for 111, per Sporting News (Sep 13). The win avenges India’s 2024 final defeat to the same opponents and extends their record to eight Asia Cup titles.

stories.headline: Bond Rout Deepens: 10-Year Yield “Will Break Above 5% in Very Short Order”
stories.body: BMO Capital Markets’ Ian Lyngen said the 10-year Treasury yield — already at its highest since 2023 — will clear 5% imminently, while Brandywine Global’s Tracy Chen said flatly “the Fed is behind the curve,” per reporting (Sep 13) as traders price high odds of a rate move at this week’s FOMC meeting. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back a day earlier, insisting “the market remains in very good shape” despite the fastest yield climb since 2007.

stories.headline: Larry Ellison Scraps $7.5 Billion Oracle Stock Sale Plan
stories.body: Oracle’s billionaire founder canceled a plan to sell up to 50 million shares that he had adopted in June; Oracle said “no Oracle stock was sold under that plan, and he has no other plans to sell any of his Oracle stock,” per Bloomberg (Sep 12). The disclosure came alongside news that Oracle’s workforce-reduction costs have swelled to $2.8 billion, $700 million more than previously estimated, even as the company rides last week’s blowout cloud-revenue results.

stories.headline: Boeing Reaches Tentative Deal With 17,000 Engineers, Averting Strike Threat
stories.body: Boeing and the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace (SPEEA) struck a tentative four-year contract offering a 10% wage increase effective October 16, plus 4% annual raises through 2030, per reporting (Sep 12). Boeing VP Ben Nimmergut said the offer “addresses the top priorities identified by our employees,” while SPEEA’s bargaining team called it “a real step forward,” after members had rejected an earlier 3% offer in August.

stories.headline: Anthropic to Buy $13.7 Billion in GPU Capacity From Tether-Linked RUM Group
stories.body: Anthropic agreed to purchase roughly $13.7 billion in GPU computing services from RUM Group over six years for a Georgia data center, in three tranches of about $4.57 billion each, per The Information via TECHi (Sep 13). Anthropic also received a warrant for up to 50.8 million RUM Group Class A shares — about 18% of that share class — at a penny each, even as RUM Group, majority-owned by Tether co-founder Giancarlo Devasini, disclosed in an SEC filing that “we do not currently have financing to fund these expenditures.”

stories.headline: Nadella Joins ‘Pace the Frontier’ Chorus as Labs Reveal Secret Standards-Body Talks
stories.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella backed calls for independent AI evaluators and “deliberate pacing,” saying “any pursuit of superintelligence has to be grounded in the core principle that if the AI we build is not helping humanity and under human control, it’s not worth pursuing,” per Business Standard (Sep 14). The same day, a report revealed Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have held private working-group talks since July, building on Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis’s proposal for a FINRA-style Frontier AI Standards Body, though the labs reportedly still disagree on how much government involvement it should have.

stories.headline: Former EPA Officials Warn AI Data Center Boom Could Cost $20.9B and 1,300 Lives a Year
stories.body: A group of former EPA officials, including 48-year agency veteran Walter Mugdan and former Air Program Director Dr. Dan Costa, projected that pollution from the AI data center buildout could cause up to $20.9 billion in annual public health costs and roughly 1,300 premature deaths a year by 2030, plus over 600,000 added asthma cases, per Hoodline (Sep 12). The report ties the risk to a roughly 25% EPA staffing cut since January 2025, with former official Lynn Goldman warning the AI expansion “can have enormous consequences for America’s health” absent stronger oversight of the data centers now operating.

stories.headline: Oman Postpones Hormuz Summit Indefinitely as Drone and Vessel Attacks Escalate
stories.body: Oman indefinitely postponed a Salalah summit meant to bring Iran, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and other Gulf states together over the Strait of Hormuz standoff, after drone strikes hit Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and Iranian and transiting vessels were attacked near Qeshm Island hours before the announcement, per The Week (Sep 14). Omani FM Sayyid Badr Albusaidi said the delay came “in the interests of consensus,” while Gulf splits remain stark: the UAE is pursuing quiet diplomacy with Tehran, Bahrain refuses any collective meeting with Iran before ties resume, and Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi maintains Tehran “would not reopen the strait until Washington lifted sanctions.”

stories.headline: Yemen’s Government Forces Counterattack as Houthis Strike Saudi Base
stories.body: Days after Houthi fighters seized Mokha and the Bab el-Mandeb’s Mayun Island, Yemen’s internationally recognized government launched Red Sea coast counterattacks after what it called a “painful” defeat, per AP (Sep 13). Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed drone and missile strikes on a Saudi military base near the border, triggering air-raid sirens in southern Saudi cities, while the UN says more than 80,000 people have been displaced since September began.

stories.headline: Russian Drone Hits Train Near Poland Border as Trump Presses Zelenskyy on Refinery Strikes
stories.body: A Russian drone struck a passenger train roughly 2km from Ukraine’s border with NATO member Poland, with a truck also hit near the Dorohusk–Yahodyn crossing; Polish FM Radosław Sikorski called the pattern of strikes near NATO territory “an escalation,” per reporting (Sep 14). Separately, President Trump urged President Zelenskyy to halt Ukrainian strikes on Russian diesel refineries such as Slavyansk-on-Kuban, arguing they are driving up global fuel costs, even as Russia struck Ukrainian power infrastructure.

stories.headline: Kushner Says US Used Israel’s Doha Isolation to Force Gaza Deal
stories.body: Jared Kushner told the Yalta European Security Conference that Israel’s strike on Hamas leaders in Doha was “a terrible thing” militarily but that Washington exploited the resulting “global isolation” to push Israel into the Gaza ceasefire, per Times of Israel (Sep 13). Netanyahu’s Likud party fired back, crediting the prime minister’s decision to strike Hamas leadership and the IDF push into Gaza City — not the Doha fallout — with forcing Hamas to drop its demands.

fixtures.headline: Man City Host Sunderland Looking to Build on Derby Win
fixtures.body: Fresh off their 10-man derby victory, Manchester City welcome newly-promoted Sunderland to the Etihad as they try to open daylight at the top of the Premier League table.

fixtures.headline: India’s White-Ball Season Opens Against West Indies
fixtures.body: India begin their home season against West Indies, with three ODIs followed by five T20Is — a long white-ball assignment ahead of India’s next major tournament cycle.

fixtures.headline: Azerbaijan GP Brings Baku’s Street-Circuit Chaos
fixtures.body: Formula 1 heads to the Baku street circuit for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, a notoriously unpredictable venue where Antonelli will look to defend his 81-point title lead over Verstappen and Norris.

portfolio.headline: Nvidia in Talks to Anchor Anthropic’s Landmark IPO With Up to $10 Billion
portfolio.body: Nvidia is in discussions to invest as much as $10 billion in Anthropic’s initial public offering as an anchor investor, per Reuters reporting carried by Yahoo Finance (Sep 11). Anthropic is reportedly seeking roughly $100 billion in the offering at a valuation near $2 trillion, which would rank among the largest IPOs ever, months after the AI lab raised $65 billion in a May funding round.

portfolio.headline: Rackspace Unveils Palantir-Powered ‘Institutional Sovereign Pod’
portfolio.body: Rackspace unveiled its “Institutional Sovereign Pod,” combining Nvidia Blackwell GPU hardware with Palantir’s Foundry and AIP software for defense, financial and government clients that need data sovereignty, per Parameter (Sep 10) — building on its new membership in Nvidia’s Cloud Partner Program announced earlier this month. CEO Gajen Kandiah said the pod targets institutions that need AI infrastructure without ceding control of sensitive data.

portfolio.headline: Intel Prices $20 Billion Share Offering as Nvidia Discloses ~$30 Billion Stake
portfolio.body: Intel priced a $20 billion common stock offering, with roughly $19.7 billion earmarked for capex, working capital and its technology and manufacturing roadmap, per StocksToTrade (Sep 8). Nvidia separately disclosed a stake in Intel valued at roughly $30 billion, deepening the chipmakers’ partnership weeks after Apple and Intel reached a preliminary chip-manufacturing agreement.

portfolio.headline: Google Closes $1.5 Billion-Plus Talent Deal for AI Startup Mechanize
portfolio.body: Google completed a deal worth more than $1.5 billion for AI coding startup Mechanize, bringing co-founder Tamay Besiroglu and more than a dozen staffers into DeepMind’s coding research team, per reporting (Sep 13). The hires will focus on AI model “midtraining” efforts, marking a sharp up-round from Mechanize’s roughly $500 million valuation earlier this year.

portfolio.headline: Palantir Price Target Raised to $250 as D.A. Davidson Cites AI Sovereignty Demand
portfolio.body: D.A. Davidson lifted its price target on Palantir to $250 from $200 while keeping a Buy rating, per a report (Sep 11), pointing to rising client demand for “AI sovereignty” tools showcased at the company’s AIPCon11 event, including a supply-chain partnership with Nvidia built on Nemotron technology. The firm cited Palantir’s recent 79% revenue growth and 85% gross margin as supporting the bullish case.

portfolio.headline: Wedbush Names CrowdStrike a Top Cybersecurity Pick, Sets $250 Target
portfolio.body: Wedbush named CrowdStrike among its highest-conviction cybersecurity picks with an Outperform rating and a $250 price target, per a report (Sep 11), citing its leadership in AI-enhanced endpoint security and autonomous security agents. The firm called it a preferred technology pick for the next 12-18 months alongside Palo Alto Networks.

portfolio.headline: PayPal’s New CEO Charts Standalone Turnaround After Buyout Talks Collapse
portfolio.body: After Stripe and Advent International walked away from a roughly $53 billion buyout proposal in late August, PayPal CEO Enrique Lores laid out a go-it-alone turnaround plan, per a report (Sep 10), centered on a $1.5 billion cost-savings initiative and a $6 billion share buyback program. The plan aims to consolidate legacy platforms including Braintree, Hyperwallet and PayPal Complete Payments, with results expected by 2027.

portfolio.headline: Piper Sandler Initiates Arm at Overweight With $320 Price Target
portfolio.body: Piper Sandler began coverage of Arm Holdings with an Overweight rating and a $320 price target, one of the highest on the Street, per MarketBeat’s analyst-ratings tracker (Sep 9). The call follows Arm’s recent unveiling of its Neoverse CSS N4 and Arm AGI CPU designs aimed at data-center and AI infrastructure customers.

stories.headline: Four Killed in Manipur Attacks on Kuki ‘Black Day’
stories.body: Gunmen struck villages in Manipur’s Tamenglong district in two pre-dawn attacks on September 13, killing four people and injuring a six-year-old boy, per WION (Sep 13). The violence fell on “Sahit Ni,” the day the Kuki community marks victims of 1990s ethnic clashes, and comes amid Meitei–Kuki tensions that have killed over 300 people since May 2023; a local village body called the strikes a “deliberate and malicious attempt to create disharmony.”

stories.headline: Modi Tells BRICS Leaders to Turn ‘Files to Real-Life Impact’
stories.body: Closing the BRICS summit he hosted in New Delhi, PM Modi pressed the bloc’s leaders — including Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian — to convert agreements into “tangible, time-bound actions,” per Fortune (Sep 13). “BRICS is not merely a group of countries, but an ecosystem of solutions,” Modi said, warning that “pandemics, climate disasters and supply-chain disruptions” show no crisis stays confined to one region; the summit also agreed to a joint early-warning system for infectious diseases.

stories.headline: Amit Shah Sets 2029 Deadline for Uniform Civil Code Rollout
stories.body: Home Minister Amit Shah said the BJP-led NDA will implement the Uniform Civil Code — replacing religion-based personal laws on marriage, divorce, inheritance and adoption — across all 21 NDA-run states before 2029, per WION (Sep 13). “I am confident that we will implement the UCC in all 21 states governed by the BJP-led NDA before 2029,” Shah said, also citing 7.8% Q1 GDP growth and unveiling a month-long “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan” campaign from Sep 17 to Oct 17.

stories.headline: Scotland, Wales & Northern Ireland Leaders to Sign Independence Pact in Cardiff
stories.body: SNP leader John Swinney, Plaid Cymru leader Rhun ap Iorwerth and Sinn Féin’s Michelle O’Neill signed a memorandum of understanding in Cardiff pressing Westminster for independence referendums, per ITV News (Sep 13). Plaid Cymru’s ap Iorwerth said the nations are “talking about how we can work together” on a different approach from the UK Government, while Scottish Education Secretary Mairi McAllan called a referendum “the transformational change that allows Scotland to stand on its own two feet.”

stories.headline: Reform UK Defends Record £72m Crypto Windfall Amid Calls for Donor Cap
stories.body: Reform UK received £72 million within 24 hours from crypto entrepreneurs Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo — the largest donations in British political history, equal to three-quarters of the party’s total spending at the 2024 election — per ITV News (Sep 13). Nigel Farage said the money would be used “to make certain we are ready to form government,” while Transparency International UK’s Duncan Hames warned “at this rate just two people could end up buying our democracy before the next election.”

stories.headline: US Diplomat Secretly Flown Out of UK Amid Child Abuse Image Probe
stories.body: US authorities reportedly raided a diplomat’s London flat in late August and removed him from Britain without formal extradition, after the Metropolitan Police opened an investigation into suspected offences involving indecent images of children, per reporting (Sep 13). The Met said “US authorities made us aware of an investigation” on August 25, while a US Embassy spokesperson said it takes the allegations “seriously” and expects staff to meet “the highest standards of conduct.”

stories.headline: Qatar’s Green Space Push Hits 94% Completion
stories.body: Qatar’s Ministry of Municipality has completed 94% of its National Strategy for Open and Recreational Areas, part of a wider push on green corridors and sports facilities under Qatar National Vision 2030, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 13). Related projects are further along still — the GCC Design Standards Manual and Green Roof Planning Standards Manual are both 100% complete, while the Smart Rainwater Monitoring Project stands at 99.8%.

stories.headline: Qatar Adds HPV Shot to School Vaccination Drive for 75,000 Students
stories.body: Qatar’s Ministry of Public Health is adding the HPV vaccine to its National School Vaccination Campaign, reaching over 75,000 students in grades 8–10 across 301 schools, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 13). Phase one runs September 20 to November 18, giving first doses to Grade 9 students and tetanus boosters to Grade 10, with health officials citing the vaccine’s over 90% efficacy when given at ages 11–14.

doha_events.headline: Tchaikovsky Takes the Stage at QNCC Tonight
doha_events.body: The Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra performs Tchaikovsky’s Piano Concerto No. 1 and Manfred Symphony tonight at QNCC Auditorium 3, with pianist Jae Hong Park and conductor Enrique Diemecke.

doha_events.headline: Uzbekistan’s 1,300-Year Legacy Lands at MIA
doha_events.body: “Uzbekistan: Heritage in Motion” brings 146 objects — manuscripts, textiles and ceramics spanning the 8th century to today — to the Museum of Islamic Art’s Sheikh Saoud Al Thani gallery through November 28.

doha_events.headline: Qatar Classic Squash Serves Up Its Second Round
doha_events.body: The QTerminals Qatar Classic Squash 2026 continues at Khalifa International Tennis & Squash Complex through September 18, with the world’s top men’s and women’s players competing for the title.

doha_events.headline: Mariachi Meets Symphony for Qatar–Mexico Year of Culture
doha_events.body: The Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra celebrates the Qatar–Mexico Year of Culture with “Sounds of Mexico” on September 18 at QNCC Auditorium 3, spotlighting Mexican musical traditions.

doha_events.headline: Taha Desouky Gets Personal at Al Mayassa Theatre
doha_events.body: Egyptian comedian Taha Desouky brings his “Let’s Make It Personal!” stand-up show to Al Mayassa Theatre, QNCC, on September 17, with doors at 9pm.
